rules.quote: Academic Research Paper Template
rules.enforcement: Template identity; all subsequent rules derive from this document.

rules.quote: Title: (Concise and informative, accurately reflecting the content of the paper)
rules.enforcement: Title length and specificity enforced on every generated manuscript.

rules.quote: • The title should be specific, accurately summarizing the study.
rules.enforcement: Title must contain a keyword from the evidence-derived keyword set.

rules.quote: • Avoid vague terms; be precise and use keywords that enhance discoverability.
rules.enforcement: Vague-term blocklist rejected in titles (deterministic + model drafts).

rules.quote: • Consider framing the title to reflect the research question or main finding.
rules.enforcement: Deterministic title embeds the candidate method and an evidence-derived keyword.

rules.quote: General Writing Guidelines:
rules.enforcement: Section header; guidelines below.

rules.quote: • Follow the PEER structure: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Repeat/Link .
rules.enforcement: Introduction and Literature Review paragraphs follow Point/Evidence/Explanation/Repeat-Link; deterministic builder emits labeled PEER blocks; model-writer system prompt mandates PEER.

rules.quote: • Use active voice for clarity and engagement.
rules.enforcement: Not deterministically enforceable; model-writer prompt instructs active voice; prose audit reports passive tell density.

rules.quote: • Maintain logical flow and coherence between sections.
rules.enforcement: Enforced structurally via section order check.

rules.quote: • Support claims with credible sources and properly cite them.
rules.enforcement: Every in-text citation key must exist in the BibTeX built from stored paper metadata; unknown keys rejected.

rules.quote: • Ensure conciseness and precision in language while avoiding unnecessary
rules.enforcement: Deterministic prose is assembled from evidence fields; prose audit flags tell-density.

rules.quote: jargon.
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the conciseness guideline.

rules.quote: Recommended Writing Order: Follow the Inside-Out Writing Method :
rules.enforcement: Inside-Out Writing Method enforced: methodology, results, discussion built before introduction/abstract/title; emission order recorded in template_audit.json.

rules.quote: • Start with Methods (easiest to write as it describes what was done).
rules.enforcement: Methodology content assembled first in the inside-out order.

rules.quote: • Move to Results (simply report the findings).
rules.enforcement: Results content assembled second in the inside-out order.

rules.quote: • Write the Discussion (interpret findings in relation to existing research).
rules.enforcement: Discussion content assembled third in the inside-out order.

rules.quote: • Complete the Introduction and Abstract together (ensuring alignment with the
rules.enforcement: Introduction and abstract assembled after results/discussion, both composed from already-built sections.

rules.quote: full paper).
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the inside-out rule.

rules.quote: Abstract: (150-250 words summarizing the research problem, methods, key findings,
rules.enforcement: Complete manuscripts must have an abstract of 150-250 words; fail-closed otherwise.

rules.quote: and conclusion)
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the abstract word-count rule.

rules.quote: • Background: Why is this topic relevant now? What is the big debate or concern?
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Background'.

rules.quote: • Gap in Knowledge: What is missing from current research?
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Gap in Knowledge'.

rules.quote: • Study Contr ibution: How does your study address this gap?
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Contribution'.

rules.quote: • Population & Methods: Outline study design, inclusion criteria, and data
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Population & Methods'.

rules.quote: sources.
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the Population & Methods part.

rules.quote: • Results: Key findings that are emphasized in the discussion.
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Results'.

rules.quote: • Conclusion: Main takeaway and implications for future research.
rules.enforcement: Abstract must contain the labeled part 'Conclusion'.

rules.quote: Keywords: (3-6 relevant terms for indexing and searching)
rules.enforcement: Keywords block with 3-6 terms, derived ONLY from Findings Memory keywords and paper metadata.

rules.quote: (Tip: We recommend writing a structured abstract and then ‘suturing’ it back together if
rules.enforcement: Structured (labeled) abstract generated; re-suturing for journal style is an author step.

rules.enforcement: Section must follow the template order.

rules.quote: • Study Design: Describe whether the study is qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-

rules.quote: • Sample & Eligibility: Describe study population and selection process.
rules.enforcement: Methodology field 'Sample & Eligibility' rendered from the freeze + spec splits/seeds; missing values reported as limitations.

rules.quote: • Data Analysis: Outline the analytical approach (e.g., thematic analysis,
rules.enforcement: Methodology field 'Data Analysis' rendered from the freeze + preregistered statistical plan; missing values reported as limitations.

rules.quote: 4. Results
rules.enforcement: Section must follow the template order.

rules.quote: • Present key findings concisel y. Clearly state the most important findings.
rules.enforcement: Results built from the deterministic table engine, decision gates, and statistical tests.

rules.quote: • Use visuals: Include tables, graphs, or figures where relevant to summarise the
rules.enforcement: Results must contain tables; when measurements exist, a deterministic figure (SVG + TikZ) must be generated and referenced.

rules.quote: results.
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the visuals rule.

rules.quote: • Highlight trends, patterns, or statistical outcomes. Identify recurring themes
rules.enforcement: Statistical outcomes come from the stored statistical tests and effect sizes.

rules.quote: or statistical outcomes
rules.enforcement: Continuation of the statistical-outcomes rule.

rules.quote: • Find a structure that enables your main points to emerge
rules.enforcement: Structure choice is an author step; the deterministic Results table provides the structure.

rules.quote: (Tip: Avoid interpretation in this section; focus on presenting objective data. Use clear
rules.enforcement: Results section must not contain interpretation words; blocklist rejected in deterministic and model drafts.

rules.quote: subheadings if necessary)
rules.enforcement: Subheading choice is an author step.

rules.quote: 5. Discussion
rules.enforcement: Section must follow the template order.

rules.quote: The discussion follows this structure to explain what the results mean (whereas the
rules.enforcement: Discussion structure (recap, limitations, strengths, implications) enforced; model-writer prompt mandates it.

rules.quote: • Recap of What You Found: Summarize key findings.
rules.enforcement: Discussion must contain the 'Recap of findings' subsection quoting the decision and evidence.

rules.enforcement: Discussion must list at least 3 distinct study limitations (report limitations + uncertainty + dataset bounds + unrun ablations + unspecified freeze fields).

rules.quote: 6. References
rules.enforcement: Section must follow the template order; every in-text citation appears in References and vice versa.

rules.quote: • Use appropriate citation style (APA, MLA, Chicago, etc.).
rules.enforcement: BibTeX (natbib plainnat) generated from stored paper metadata; journal-specific style is an author step.

rules.quote: • Ensure all sources cited in the text are listed here.
rules.enforcement: Bidirectional citation check: used keys subset of BibTeX keys; BibTeX built only from stored papers.

rules.quote: • Use Zotero or Endnote or another reference manager
rules.enforcement: The generated references.bib is a reference-manager import format built from stored metadata.

rules.enforcement: Appendices section always emitted for complete manuscripts, listing the evidence bundle, raw seed metrics, and exact commands.

rules.enforcement: Appendices list the evidence bundle (ids + checksums), raw seed metrics, and exact recorded commands; never empty filler.
